# strictix — shared API contract (M4–M8)

This is the exact public API that crates/core, crates/lints, and crates/cli
implement and consume. All RLMs building strictix code MUST follow these
signatures exactly. Where a name appears in this doc, use that name.

Workspace: /home/y0usaf/dev/strictix-new
- crates/syntax  (DONE, do not touch) — lexer, parser, CST, typed AST
- crates/core    (M4 + M5 in progress) — semantic model, diagnostics, fixes, rules, config
- crates/lints   (M6 + M8) — builtin rules, first customer of core's public API
- crates/cli     (M7) — entrypoint

Constraints for ALL code:
- Rust edition 2021. #![forbid(unsafe_code)] at crate root.
- NO new third-party dependencies. Blessed deps: serde + toml, and ONLY in
  crates/cli. core and lints depend only on sibling path crates.
- Follow the existing style: //! module docs, /// doc comments on every pub
  item, #[must_use] on pure accessors, one mechanism for everything (no
  hand-wired special cases).
- Diagnostics/fixes must be lossless-safe: fixes never destroy formatting.
- Parse errors never panic; rule code never panics on malformed trees.

## syntax crate public API (already exists — READ, do not modify)

Path: crates/syntax/src/{lib,kind,green,ast}.rs. Re-exports from lib.rs:
parse(source: &str) -> SyntaxNode
SyntaxKind (enum, all node kinds + token kinds; K:: alias used in tests)
SyntaxNode { kind(), range() -> TextRange, children() -> &[NodeOrToken],
  child_nodes(), child_tokens(), child_node(kind), child_nodes_of_kind(kind),
  descendants(), text(source), reassemble(source) }
SyntaxToken { kind(), range() -> TextRange, text(source) -> &str }
NodeOrToken { Node(SyntaxNode) | Token(SyntaxToken), kind(), range() }
TextRange { start(): u32, end(): u32, is_empty(), contains(offset) }
AstNode trait { cast(node) -> Option<Self>, syntax(), range() }
Typed wrappers (each with AstNode impl): Root, ErrorNode, LetExpr, LetBindings,
Binding, Attrpath, InheritStmt, WithExpr, AssertExpr, IfExpr, AttrsetExpr,
RecAttrsetExpr, Formals, ListExpr, LambdaExpr, ApplyExpr, UnaryExpr, BinExpr,
SelectExpr, HasAttrExpr, StringExpr, IndStringExpr, InterpExpr, ParenExpr.

Key accessors (read ast.rs for full list):
- Root::expr() -> Option<Expr>
- LetExpr::bindings() -> Option<LetBindings>, body() -> Option<Expr>
- LetBindings::items() -> impl Iterator<Item = AttrItem>  (Binding | Inherit)
- Binding::attrpath() -> Option<Attrpath>, value() -> Option<Expr>
- Attrpath::elements() -> impl Iterator<Item = AttrName>  (Ident(tok) | Str(StringExpr))
- InheritStmt::source() -> Option<Expr>, names() -> impl Iterator<Item = &SyntaxToken>
- WithExpr::scope() -> Option<Expr>, body() -> Option<Expr>
- AssertExpr::cond()/body(), IfExpr::cond()/then_branch()/else_branch()
- AttrsetExpr::items(), RecAttrsetExpr::attrset() -> Option<AttrsetExpr>
- Formals::params() -> impl Iterator<Item = FormalParam { name: &SyntaxToken, default: Option<Expr> }>, has_ellipsis()
- LambdaExpr::param() -> LambdaParam (Ident(&SyntaxToken) | Formals(Formals, Option<&SyntaxToken> at-name)), body()
- ListExpr::items(), ApplyExpr::func()/arg(), UnaryExpr::operand()
- BinExpr::lhs()/rhs()/op() -> Option<SyntaxKind>
- SelectExpr::base()/attrpath()/default()
- HasAttrExpr::base()/attrpath()
- StringExpr::parts(), IndStringExpr::parts() -> StringPart (Content(&SyntaxToken) | Interp(InterpExpr))
- InterpExpr::expr(), ParenExpr::expr()
- Expr enum: Ident(&SyntaxToken), Int, Float, Path, SearchPath, Uri, Let, With,
  Assert, If, Attrset, RecAttrset, List, Lambda, Apply, Unary, Bin, Select,
  HasAttr, String, IndString, Paren. Expr::cast(node), cast_token(token),
  range(), text(source).

## crates/core public API (implement this; each RLM owns its file)

### semantic.rs — M4 SemanticModel (lazy, built once per file)

pub struct SemanticModel<'a> { /* source: &'a str, root: &'a SyntaxNode,
    built: RefCell<Option<Built<'a>>> — do not expose fields */ }

pub struct Built<'a> { /* internal: scopes, bindings, references, with_sites,
    import_sites */ }

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct ScopeId(pub u32);

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum BindingKind {
    LambdaParam,   // x: ...  or a formal param in { a, b ? 1, ... }:
    AtName,        // args@{ ... }: ...
    LetBinding,    // let a = ...;  (sequential visibility: earlier entries + outer scopes)
    RecAttr,       // rec { a = ...; }  (mutually visible)
    InheritName,   // inherit (x) a b;  (bound in the containing block, per its rules)
}

pub struct Binding<'a> {
    pub name: &'a SyntaxToken,     // the defining ident token
    pub scope: ScopeId,
    pub references: Vec<TextRange>, // byte ranges of resolved uses (filled in pass 2)
}

pub struct Reference<'a> {
    pub name: &'a SyntaxToken,      // ident token used in expression position
    pub resolved: Option<usize>,    // index into model.bindings(); None if unbound lexically
    pub via_with: Option<usize>,    // index into model.with_sites() when resolved by fallback
}

pub struct WithSite {
    pub scope_range: TextRange,     // the scope expression (with e; ...)
    pub body_range: TextRange,      // everything after the ;
}

pub struct ImportSite {
    pub call_range: TextRange,      // whole import call
    pub path_range: TextRange,      // the argument (path/string/expr)
}

impl<'a> SemanticModel<'a> {
    pub fn new(source: &'a str, root: &'a SyntaxNode) -> Self;
    pub fn source(&self) -> &'a str;
    pub fn root(&self) -> &'a SyntaxNode;

    // Accessors below trigger the one-time build (RefCell<Option<Built>>),
    // then return borrowed slices. Calling them twice is cheap.
    pub fn bindings(&self) -> &[Binding<'a>];
    pub fn references(&self) -> &[Reference<'a>];
    pub fn with_sites(&self) -> &[WithSite];
    pub fn import_sites(&self) -> &[ImportSite];

    /// Resolve an ident token that belongs to this tree.
    pub fn resolve(&self, token: &SyntaxToken) -> Option<&Binding<'a>>;
    /// Nearest lexical binding visible at byte offset (no with fallback).
    pub fn resolve_lexical(&self, name: &str, offset: u32) -> Option<&Binding<'a>>;
    /// Whether any binding (lexical or with fallback) could cover name at offset.
    pub fn is_bound(&self, name: &str, offset: u32) -> bool;
}

Scope rules to implement (Nix semantics, exactly):
- Scopes: RootScope (whole file), LetScope per let, LambdaScope per lambda
  (params, formals, at-name), RecScope per rec attrset. Attrsets (non-rec) bind
  nothing for resolution. with creates a WithScope over its body only.
- Bindings in scope order: let bindings sequential (binding i visible in
  bindings i+1..n and the body; NOT in its own value, NOT in earlier values).
  inherit (x) a b; in a let adds a,b as LetBinding-kind entries at that
  position. rec attrset: all attr names visible in all values (recursion).
  formals: param i visible in defaults of j>i and in the body. at-name visible
  in the body. Lambda ident param visible in the body (NOT in itself).
  inherit (x) a b; in an attrset adds a,b as InheritName entries; in rec, as
  RecAttr entries.
- References: ident tokens in EXPRESSION position. NOT attrpath elements
  (binding position or select field), NOT keyword tokens, NOT inherit names,
  NOT formals. Interpolations ARE expression positions.
- Resolution of a reference at position P: walk scopes outward from the
  innermost scope containing P. First lexical binding whose scope rules make
  it visible at P wins (respecting let sequentiality and formals defaults).
  If NO lexical binding found on the whole path, fall back to with-scopes:
  the innermost with-scope whose body contains P is the candidate; record
  via_with = that with's index. (Statically we cannot know whether the with
  actually provides the name — via_with only records the innermost candidate.)
- import sites: ApplyExpr with func = Ident "import". Record call_range and
  path_range (the argument expr's range). Also record for builtins.import
  (func = Select with base Ident builtins and attrpath [import]).
- The model must be LAZY: SemanticModel::new does no walking. The build runs
  once (RefCell) on first accessor call and is shared thereafter.
- Malformed trees (ErrorNode regions) are handled gracefully: skip error
  nodes, never panic.

### diagnostic.rs — M5

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Severity { Warning, Error }

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Diagnostic {
    pub code: &'static str,      // rule code, kebab-case
    pub severity: Severity,
    pub message: String,
    pub range: TextRange,
    pub help: Option<String>,
    pub fix: Option<Fix>,
}

impl Diagnostic {
    pub fn new(code: &'static str, severity: Severity, message: impl Into<String>, range: TextRange) -> Self;
    pub fn with_help(mut self, help: impl Into<String>) -> Self;
    pub fn with_fix(mut self, fix: Fix) -> Self;
    pub fn severity_str(&self) -> &'static str;   // "warning" | "error"
}

### fix.rs — M5 text-splice fixes

pub struct TextEdit { pub range: TextRange, pub replacement: String }
impl TextEdit { pub fn new(range: TextRange, replacement: impl Into<String>) -> Self; }

pub struct Fix { pub label: String, pub edits: Vec<TextEdit> }
impl Fix {
    pub fn new(label: impl Into<String>) -> Self;
    pub fn edit(mut self, range: TextRange, replacement: impl Into<String>) -> Self;
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum FixError {
    Overlap(TextRange, TextRange),   // two edits whose ranges intersect
    InvalidRange(TextRange),         // range outside the source
}

/// Apply edits in reverse range order; error on overlap. Edits may arrive in
/// any order (sorted internally). Replaces each range with its replacement.
pub fn apply_fixes(source: &str, edits: &[TextEdit]) -> Result<String, FixError>;

### config.rs — M5 lint configuration

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct LintConfig {
    pub disabled: Vec<String>,        // rule codes to skip
    pub schema: Option<std::path::PathBuf>, // options.json path (M8); None = schema rule off
}
impl LintConfig {
    pub fn is_enabled(&self, code: &str) -> bool;  // true unless disabled contains code
    pub fn with_disabled(mut self, codes: impl IntoIterator<Item = String>) -> Self;
    pub fn with_schema(mut self, path: impl Into<std::path::PathBuf>) -> Self;
}

### rules.rs — M5 rule traits + one registry mechanism

pub trait Rule: Send + Sync {
    fn code(&self) -> &'static str;          // kebab-case unique id
    fn name(&self) -> &'static str;          // short human title
    fn description(&self) -> &'static str;   // what it catches and why (1-3 sentences)
    fn severity(&self) -> Severity;
    fn node_kind(&self) -> Option<SyntaxKind> { None }   // Some = node rule
    fn check_node(&self, node: &SyntaxNode, source: &str, diags: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {}
    fn check_file(&self, model: &SemanticModel, config: &LintConfig, diags: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {}
}

/// Run every enabled rule over one file. Node rules fire once per node of
/// their kind; file rules fire once with the (lazy) semantic model.
pub fn run_rules(
    rules: &[Box<dyn Rule>],
    tree: &SyntaxNode,
    model: &SemanticModel,
    config: &LintConfig,
    source: &str,
    diags: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
);

/// One declaration mechanism: a macro generating the registry.
/// Define 'rules!' here as #[macro_export] so crates/lints can use it:
///   rules! { UnusedLetBinding => "unused-let-binding", ... }
/// Your choice of syntax — document it in code. The macro must expand to a
/// Vec<Box<dyn Rule>> (each entry Box::new(Type {})).

### json.rs — M8 minimal JSON parser (hand-written, no serde_json)

pub enum JsonValue {
    Null,
    Bool(bool),
    Number(f64),
    String(String),
    Array(Vec<JsonValue>),
    Object(Vec<(String, JsonValue)>),   // insertion order preserved
}
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct JsonError { pub message: String, pub offset: usize }

impl JsonValue {
    /// Parse a complete JSON document. Full spec: strings with escapes
    /// (quote-backslash-slash-b-f-n-r-t and \uXXXX incl. surrogate pairs),
    /// numbers (int, fraction, exponent), true/false/null, arrays, objects,
    /// arbitrary whitespace. Rejects trailing non-whitespace.
    pub fn parse(input: &str) -> Result<JsonValue, JsonError>;
    pub fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&JsonValue>;         // object lookup
    pub fn as_str(&self) -> Option<&str>;
    pub fn as_bool(&self) -> Option<bool>;
    pub fn as_array(&self) -> Option<&[JsonValue]>;
    pub fn as_object(&self) -> Option<&[(String, JsonValue)]>;
}

## crates/lints public API (M6 + M8)

lib.rs:
pub fn all_rules() -> Vec<Box<dyn Rule>>;   // the whole registry, via the rules! macro

Node rules (node_rules.rs, each a struct implementing Rule with node_kind()
Some and check_node()):
1. constant-if      — IfExpr whose cond is the literal true or false.
   Fix for true: replace whole if-expr with then-branch text; for false:
   replace with else-branch text. Message: "constant condition in if".
2. assert-true      — AssertExpr whose cond is literal true. Fix: remove
   the assert true; prefix (range from assert start through the ;).
   Message: "assert true is always satisfied".
3. tautology        — BinExpr x == x, x != x, x && x, x || x. No fix.
   Message: "tautological comparison".

File rules (file_rules.rs, check_file() using the SemanticModel):
4. unused-let-binding — LetBinding kind with zero references. Fix: remove
   the whole binding statement. Message: "binding 'x' is never used".
5. unused-lambda-param — LambdaParam::Ident params with zero references and
   name not starting with '_'. No fix. Message: "parameter 'x' is never used".
6. unused-formal — formal params with zero references, name not starting
   with '_', ONLY when the lambda's formals have NO ellipsis. No fix.
7. shadowed-binding — any binding whose name has a visible outer lexical
   binding at its position (model.resolve_lexical). Message: "binding 'x'
   shadows an outer binding".
8. redundant-with — WithSite whose body references ALL resolve lexically
   (every reference inside body_range has resolved = Some(_) and
   via_with = None). Message: "with-scope is never used".
9. self-referential-let — LetBinding whose value expression contains an
   ident reference with the binding's own name that resolves to nothing
   (model.is_bound(name, offset) is false). This is the 'let x = x;'
   infinite-recursion AI slop. Message: "binding 'x' references itself:
   infinite recursion".

Schema rule (schema.rs, M8): 'unknown-option' — a FileRule that activates
only when config.schema is Some. It loads+parses options.json once (rules are
long-lived; use std::sync::OnceLock in the rule struct), collects the set of
valid option paths ("services.example.enable" etc. — options.json shape:
{"options": {"a.b.c": {...}}}), then walks the model: find references to a
binding named "config" whose kind is LambdaParam (a NixOS module argument);
for each such reference, examine the surrounding SelectExpr chains
(config.services.example.enable) and record each full attrpath text; flag any
attrpath NOT present in the options set as unknown-option. Range = the select
chain's attrpath range. Message: "option 'services.exmaple.enable' is not
declared in options.json".

## Rendering contract (used by CLI and by lints snapshot tests)

Deterministic one-line diagnostic format (tests use this):
  [{code}] {severity} {start}..{end} {message}
e.g.  [unused-let-binding] warning 10..23 binding 'x' is never used

CLI human format (render.rs in cli):
  {path}:{line}:{col}: {severity}[{code}]: {message}
then for each diagnostic, the source line with a caret line, then optional
help line. line/col are 1-based, computed from source.

## M7 CLI commands (cli crate: main.rs + modules args.rs walk.rs config.rs render.rs)

strictix check [PATH...]       lint files or directories (default: .)
strictix fix [PATH...]         lint + apply automatic fixes (writes files)
strictix explain CODE          print a rule's details
strictix list                  list all rules
Flags: -h/--help, -V/--version, --config FILE (TOML), --format human|json,
--ignore-file FILE (default .strictixignore), --disable CODE (repeatable),
--schema FILE (options.json, enables unknown-option).

Exit codes: 0 clean (or help/version/list/explain), 1 diagnostics found or
any error.

check walks paths (std::thread::scope workers, one per file), parses with
strictix_syntax::parse, builds SemanticModel, runs all_rules() via
core::rules::run_rules, renders. fix applies apply_fixes per file, writes
files back only when changed, prints per-file change counts.

.strictixignore: one pattern per line, '#' comments, blank lines ignored.
Pattern without '/' matches any path component; with '/' matches relative to
the walk root. '*' wildcard within a component. Default skip list: .git,
target, result, result-*.

strictix.toml (--config, default ./strictix.toml if present):
  [lint]
  disabled = ["tautology"]
  schema = "options.json"
Any other keys ignored. cli deserializes with toml+serde into its own DTO,
converts to core's LintConfig (no serde in core).

JSON output (--format json) — serde_json::json! in cli:
  {"files":[{"path": "...", "diagnostics":[{code,severity,message,
    "range":{"start":u32,"end":u32}, "help": "...", "fix": {"label":"...",
    "edits":[{"range":{"start":..,"end":..},"replacement":"..."}]}}]}],
   "summary":{"files":n,"diagnostics":n}}
severity as "warning"/"error".

## Testing conventions

- Tests live in crates/{core,lints}/tests/*.rs and cli/src (unit) + cli/tests.
- Exact-match snapshot-style tests: render diagnostics with the one-line
  format above and assert against expected string literals or per-fixture
  .txt files (tests/snapshots/*.txt, regenerated when UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1).
- Semantic model tests MUST cover: shadowing (let over let), rec self-refs,
  formals defaults referencing earlier params, at-name, inherit binding,
  with-fallback (via_with recorded), unbound reference, lazy build (model
  built only on first accessor call), import sites (import ./x and
  builtins.import), and the Nix gotcha: let binding not visible in its own
  value.
- Rules tests MUST cover each rule's positive case and 2-3 false-positive
  guards (well-formed code producing zero diagnostics).
- json.rs tests: round-trip all types, escapes, unicode surrogate pairs,
  nested structures, malformed input errors (trailing junk, unclosed braces,
  bad escapes, bare numbers in strings, NaN/Infinity rejected).
